sourcesActuallyRead.title: How to Read a Mammal Skull
sourcesActuallyRead.organisation: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
sourcesActuallyRead.readScope: Original Skull Basics, Eyes and Teeth sections actually read. They locate bony orbits in the skull and name the front-to-back tooth-row gap a diastema. Broader tendencies about orbit size, activity patterns or distance judgement are not treated as measurements of this animal.
sourcesActuallyRead.role: Anatomical interpretation of a skull; same Smithsonian family as the collection record, never counted independently from it.

sourcesActuallyRead.title: Dama dama (fallow deer), Aarti Dharmani
sourcesActuallyRead.organisation: Animal Diversity Web, academic species account
sourcesActuallyRead.readScope: Original scientific classification and species heading actually read: Dama/dama/fallow deer, within Cervidae. The new wrong species alternative is a different named taxon from the museum's Odocoileus virginianus. Old source subspecies treatment, dimensions, ranges, phenology and behavioural generalisations are excluded.
sourcesActuallyRead.role: Independent taxonomy/context only; does not relabel or independently identify EO404749.

sourcesActuallyRead.title: Anatomy and Physiology2e,14.1 Sensory Perception, Vision
sourcesActuallyRead.readScope: Actual original Vision/Retina paragraphs around web lines181–185 and193–194 read. They distinguish the eye's neural retina and light-responsive receptor cells from surrounding structures. Only that structure/function distinction is used; the textbook's human-specific fovea, cone classes, numerical physiology and clinical applications are not transferred to deer.
sourcesActuallyRead.role: Independent anatomical/physiological context for why an empty bony orbit is not a direct retinal-function observation. The absence of a function measurement in this particular cast follows from its actual data/provenance, not from a newly performed eye test.

sourcesActuallyRead.title: Mammal Glossary
sourcesActuallyRead.organisation: University of Texas at El Paso, Laboratory for Environmental Biology
sourcesActuallyRead.readScope: Original full alveolar/diastema entries actually read. A tooth alveolus is its socket/cavity, whereas a diastema is a gap between teeth. No clinical assessment of a particular tooth or diagnosis of missing teeth is taken.
sourcesActuallyRead.role: Independent direct terminology contrast against the Smithsonian's gap definition.

questions.questionDirection: positive: identify the species explicitly assigned by the collection
questions.comparison: Dama dama is not the curator-assigned Odocoileus virginianus. The candidate is a familiar other cervid without using antler form or a photograph to invent a new identification.
questions.existingTeaching: All3model scientificName fields and the main museum boundary name the North American white-tailed deer, not a native roe/red deer. The old full explanation remains exact.
questions.limit: No new origin/range/age assertion; do not claim the independent species account inspected these particular casts.

questions.questionDirection: positive: distinguish direct bony observation from a living-eye property
questions.comparison: The cast shows orbit location. A retinal light-response property is not directly visible in that bony shape, just as the old choices already exclude exact acuity and eye colour.
questions.existingTeaching: augenhoehle already explicitly limits inference from the skull to individual vision; nasenraum also distinguishes bone from missing mucosal soft tissue.
questions.limit: No value for sensitivity, no claim of poor/good vision in this animal, no human foveal anatomy or numbers transferred to deer.

questions.questionDirection: positive: choose the name of the tooth-free interval, not the socket of a tooth
questions.comparison: Diastema denotes the interval between tooth groups in this teaching example; an alveolus is the socket associated with an individual tooth. This is a plausible neighbouring anatomical term, distinct from the old horn-pedicle/ear-canal distractors.
questions.existingTeaching: diastema already calls the gap a normal structural feature rather than automatic tooth loss. The original definition/explanation and model camera remain untouched.
questions.limit: No dental-age judgement, disease conclusion, fracture interpretation or claim that every apparent gap is a normal diastema.

questions.questionDirection: positive: identify an actual limitation of this bone cast
questions.fourthChoice: Fehlende Muskeln werden beim Drehen automatisch ergänzt
questions.comparison: The recorded object is a bone cast, and camera-orbit changes the view of the loaded data. In the actual unchanged cast files/component there is no source of reconstructed missing musculature. This is a bounded inference about these exact models, not a general ban on anatomical software having additional layers.
questions.existingTeaching: kieferast already says muscles/cartilage are not shown, and the old question explanation explicitly lists missing living soft-tissue structures.
questions.limit: Do not claim model-viewer certifies biological completeness or that all3Dsoftware cannot reconstruct tissue. No new model or reconstruction is proposed.

questions.questionDirection: positive: choose whether these views are a valid same-scale comparison
questions.fourthChoice: Ja, wenn beide Modelle ihr Ansichtsfenster ganz ausfüllen
questions.comparison: The curator expressly warns that skull/forelimb may be from different specimens and are not to common scale. Camera framing is based on each loaded model and window; equal viewport filling does not overturn that warning.
questions.existingTeaching: massstab and the original question explanation already separate displayed size from bodily size. This fourth option checks the actual fit-to-window misunderstanding without changing model units.
questions.limit: No physical size, conversion factor or altered GLB scale; no claim that metric geometry is impossible in the file format.

questions.questionDirection: positive: identify the actual digital teaching medium
questions.comparison: The collection identifies scanned physical casts. The tool loads those exactGLB3Dassets and exposes camera orbit; the local source files have no animation data. A change of viewpoint is not a recorded motion sequence of a living limb.
questions.existingTeaching: The existing Vorderlauf description explains the arranged cast parts and explicitly says their spacing is not live joint movement. The old scan explanation already rules out reconstructing missing tissue/movement.
questions.limit: No walking sequence, muscle-force measurement, live scan or medical-imaging claim; only this static cast model's documented identity is contrasted with film.
